static_traits.name: Li Man
static_traits.family_status: Has two children, living in Louisiana, practicing Hinduism; mother good at baking
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive mother and some friends, but hesitant to express guilt and self-blame
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness history; has not yet received psychotherapy or psychological treatment before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, acceptable logic; negative tone, often describing self with self-blame and failure labels; able to identify automatic thoughts and try more balanced expressions; good cooperativeness

basic_info.main_problem: I feel I am a terrible wife, because I have two children yet divorced; this thinking leads to guilt and self-blame.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these feelings of guilt and self-blame have begun to affect my academic performance and daily functioning.
growth_experiences: Two years ago she went through a divorce; the breakup of the marriage and family brought high pressure and strong emotions; since then she has long been troubled by guilt and self-blame, persistently believing she failed in the marriage, affecting self-esteem and overall mood, in turn interfering with academic performance, daily tasks and self-care, and leading to difficulties in building new interpersonal/intimate relationships.

core_beliefs: I am not a competent partner/mother

special_situations.event: Recalling the divorce and past marriage experiences
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot maintain my marriage, it proves I am a failed partner
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Buries my energy in studies and uses self-criticism to 'supervise' myself to make up for failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am just a terrible wife / I am a failure

special_situations.event: Trying to build new relationships or talk to others about the divorce
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others know I am divorced, they will look down on me or reject me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids socializing and self-disclosure; reducing deep communication with family and friends
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am unworthy and untrustworthy

special_situations.event: When facing academic pressure or noticing grades being affected
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my studies are not perfect enough, it means I am worthless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling down on learning; burying oneself in tasks to control anxiety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My life is going downhill; I will keep failing forever

special_situations.event: Thinking about the broken family when with the child
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the child is affected by the divorce, it is all my personal fault
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Excessive self-blame, compensating for perceived indebtedness through more companionship
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I made the child suffer; this is my responsibility

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be seen as a competent, accepted partner and mother, with a stable intimate relationship and sense of self-worth
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged a failure again, being rejected, worrying about hurting the children or repeating relationship breakdown
defense_goal: Lowering the risk of being judged and rejected by avoiding new relationships and suppressing expression
Maintains a sense of control and compensates for feelings of failure through self-criticism

object_relations.self_representation: A failed wife / an incompetent mother
object_relations.object_representation: Others (potential partners, family and friends) are critics/judges

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When considering building a new relationship or confiding about the divorce experience
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing the other will judge oneself like society or the ex did (transference: projecting self-shame onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a vague and reserved tone; reducing self-disclosure; avoiding deep discussion of feelings; shifting to neutral topics or ending the conversation.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to weigh positive and negative evidence and try a more balanced self-statement
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Viewing reframing as 'making excuses for oneself', worrying it will make one irresponsible
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing divorce as decisive evidence; using rigid 'should/must' phrasing to negate positive examples; harsh tone, holding the self-blaming stance.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about divorce and children and emotions well up
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes expressing emotion will burden others or make them lose control, so emotion and aggression are turned back onto the self
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expressing in self-deprecating, apologetic language; avoiding naming external factors and real constraints; reinforcing self-blame and ending the topic.

manifestations: Feeling ashamed and like a failure long after divorce; hesitating to express emotions to the support system (mother and friends)
Hard to build new relationships, worries about being judged and rejected

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection with excessive self-restriction and reproach, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequently labeling oneself as 'failure / bad wife'
Overly concerned about others' possible evaluations, reducing self-disclosure and help-seeking

contact_model.definition: The individual turns the energy originally meant to be directed outward back onto themselves, restraining expression or seeking help from others.
manifestations: Feeling ashamed and not talking about guilt and self-blame with mother and friends
Repressing emotions by doubling down on studies; bearing it alone

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Believing others will look down on oneself (divorced, has two children)
Avoiding contact out of worry about being rejected or judged in new relationships

exception_events.target_problem: When reflecting on divorce and past relationships, the client usually falls into rumination on 'I am a failure / terrible wife', low mood, and difficulty focusing on learning.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In some moments with the children, the client has not yet fallen into self-blame, being able to feel 'I am a good mom' and connect more deeply with the children.
exception_events.reason: Clue: different situations and focuses — focusing attention on the children's immediate needs and interactions, positive experiences and a sense of value emerge, briefly deviating from the failure narrative.

exception_events.target_problem: In academic pressure situations, the client usually has scattered attention and declining performance due to negative self-evaluation.
exception_events.unique_outcome: The client performed well in some courses and received positive feedback, experiencing a sense of achievement.
exception_events.reason: Clue: different approaches — investing in concrete tasks, gaining positive feedback; although emotional distress persisted, clearer tasks and greater engagement led to better outcomes.

positive_force: Has a supportive mother and friends (a potential support network)
Having already performed well in some courses, with the ability to invest in learning and gain feedback
Can experience 'good mother' moments and a sense of value in close interactions with the child
Willing to try more balanced self-statements and cognitive reframing (such as 'I tried my best, but did not succeed')
negative_force: Rigid self-labeling and overgeneralization (equating divorce with total failure)
Guilt and self-blame maintaining rumination, negating positive evidence and experiences
Mind reading of others' evaluations and negative predictions, leading to avoidance of new relationships and help-seeking
Impaired self-esteem and strong shame, lowering self-acceptance and expression
Catastrophizing and negative anticipation under academic pressure; attention and functioning impaired

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated self-labeling and rumination with guilt-laden self-blame ('I am a failure / terrible wife')
antecedent: Recalling the divorce and past relationships
Facing academic pressure or noticing grades being affected
Trying to build new relationships or discuss the divorce with others
When with her children, thinks about the family breakdown and what she owes
target_behavior.core_reason: Treating divorce as total negation of self-worth; maintaining the failure narrative with catastrophizing, overgeneralization, mind reading, and negating-the-positive cognitive biases.
target_behavior.function: Escaping uncertainty and outside judgment; gaining short-term control and self-punishing 'compensation', while avoiding being hurt again.
target_behavior.consequence: Impaired self-esteem and low mood; academic and daily task execution blocked; interpersonal avoidance, difficulty building new relationships.
